title: Hourly negative-shock overreaction: buy 4h crash close above SMA1200, 24h hold
ex_ante_rule: Closed 1h candles only; signal evaluated at bar close t, order executed at the next bar open (t+1). Long only, one position per pair, whole allowed balance, no pyramiding, no take-profit, no sizing hooks, no other filters. Definition: r4(t) = close(t)/close(t-4) - 1. ENTRY at close of bar t when ALL hold: (1) r4(t) <= -0.04; (2) close(t) > SMA(1200) of close at t (not a long-term downtrend); (3) no open position; (4) cooldown satisfied. Pre-drop price P = close(t-4), stored at signal time. EXIT (signal at a bar close, executed at the next open) when the first of these occurs: (a) close >= P (pre-drop price regained); (b) 24 bars have elapsed since the signal bar t (close of bar t+24, executed at open of t+25). STOP-LOSS: one fixed percentage, 5% below the entry price, as the engine's native intrabar stop (triggers as soon as price touches it, not on a close). COOLDOWN: no re-entry for 12 candles after any exit. All thresholds fixed in advance and not tuned: shock window 4 bars, shock threshold -4.0%, trend SMA 1200 bars, max hold 24 bars, stop 5%, cooldown 12 bars. Warm-up: 1200 bars (SMA(1200); no recursive indicators; set startup_candle_count to 1200 or slightly more, at most 4500).

parameters.stop_type: native intrabar fixed percentage below entry
parameters.execution: next bar open after signal close

rationale: Mechanism: forced sellers (liquidations, stop cascades, panic market orders) push price below fair value within a few hours; liquidity providers and patient buyers are paid to absorb that flow as price relaxes back over roughly 6-24 hours. The cited paper reports overreaction after negative intraday Bitcoin shocks that grows over hours; it gives no explicit rule, so the thresholds here are my own round numbers, fixed before any result, and I found no source for the exact numbers. The SMA(1200) (50 days) gate avoids buying crashes inside a sustained downtrend, where drops continue (the earlier failure pattern of long losing streaks in bear markets). Frequency: a 4% fall in 4 hours is rare for BTC/ETH/BNB, so I expect roughly 10-40 signals per pair per year (fewer on BTC); fewer than 30 trades per split is a real risk and the rule is not loosened to avoid it. Cost: round trip is 0.35% at base and 0.95% at stress; the target is a partial retracement of a 4% drop (return to pre-drop price is up to about 4%, and the 24h hold captures the relaxation), well above 0.35%, though stress cost would consume much of a typical partial recovery. The 5% stop with whole-balance sizing bounds loss per trade at about 5% plus slippage; drawdown control relies on the rarity of trades and the trend gate. Success criteria are the existing gates: positive net profit at base and conservative cost, drawdown below 25%, at least 30 trades, same rule on all three pairs.
novelty_vs_tried: All tried families are slow breakouts, daily dip rules, or trend/momentum holds with multi-day to multi-week holds. This is a short-horizon event rule: a discrete 4-hour crash shock (-4%) followed by a hold of at most 24 hours, exiting on recovery of the pre-drop price. It is not a Bollinger/RSI/EMA z-score dip (EMASnapbackATR, H-003) because the trigger is a raw 4-bar return, not a deviation from a moving average, there is no recovery confirmation bar, and the exit is a price level from before the shock plus a time stop. The SMA(1200) filter is only a crash-in-downtrend guard.

sources.title: Intraday Bitcoin price shocks: when bad news is good news (Review of Quantitative Finance and Accounting? / Taylor & Francis, via RePEc)
